Answer the question from the sources. Put the label of the passage you used in brackets after
each claim, like [P12].

Shape the answer like this:
1. The first paragraph is one sentence that answers the question outright, with its numbers. Nothing before it.
2. Then a blank line and the detail: under 120 words, in one to three short paragraphs. When more than one source
   bears on the question, bring them together: where they agree, where they differ, which source says what.
3. Only when the question needs more than that, a blank line and the rest (the reader opens it with More).

Plain words, short sentences. No headings, no bullet lists, no bold. Never coin a shorthand noun for a group of
people ("stayers", "leavers", "completers"); say "learners who stayed". Use only the passage labels shown in the
sources. If the sources don't answer it, say so in one sentence and name what is missing. Then suggest three

request.input_head:
=== SOURCE 1: FY26 Program Report (Word) ===
[P1] (“Who we served”) In fiscal year 2026, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners across five neighborhood sites, up from 936 the year before. Of those learners, 412 were working toward a high school equivalency credential and 389 were English language learners.
Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential, the most in the organization's history.
[P2] (“Volunteers and staff”) A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. The average tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight employs 11 full-time staff, including four site coordinators.
[P3] (“Money”) Operating expenses for FY2026 were $1,420,000. Program costs were 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants provided $640,000, individual donors gave $388,000, and the city's adult education contract paid $295,000.
The cost per learner was $1,237.
[P4] (“The waitlist”) At year end, 287 adults were on the waitlist, most of them at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. The average wait was nine weeks.
[P5] (“Recommendation to the board”) Staff recommend that the board approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000, which adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and two site coordinators. Staff estimate the sixth site would serve 180 more learners a year and cut the waitlist in half.

The sources don't say whether the board can afford the FY2027 budget of $1,610,000 while reserves stand at 3.2 months against a 4-month target, because they give no FY2027 revenue plan and no estimate of how the budget would affect reserves [P5][P8].

What the sources do give: operating expenses for FY2026 were $1,420,000 [P3]. That year, foundation grants provided $640,000, individual donors gave $388,000, and the city's adult education contract paid $295,000 [P3]. Staff recommend the $1,610,000 budget. It would add a sixth site and two site coordinators [P5]. The treasurer reported that reserves are below the board's target [P8].

The board agreed to vote on the budget on October 21 [P8]. The notes don't record the result. To answer the question, you would need projected FY2027 revenue, a plan to pay for the sixth site, and the effect on reserves.
